citation: Yang, R., Porter, A. C., Massey, C. M., Merlino, J. F., & Desimone, L. M. (2020). Curriculum-based teacher professional development in middle school science: A comparison of training focused on cognitive science principles versus content knowledge. Journal of Research in Science Teaching, 57(4), 536-566.
report_number: DOI 10.1002/tea.21605; ERIC EJ1246516; IES grant R305C080009 (National R&D Center on Cognition and Science Instruction)
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT; 90 middle schools randomized to 3 arms (Cohort 1 = 90 schools/145 teachers/6410 students; Cohort 2 = 82 schools/130 teachers/5508 students). THREE arms: (a) Content = PD to improve teacher science content knowledge [= row 142, (P)CK/content-knowledge arm]; (b) Cog-sci = Holt textbook curriculum modified per four cognitive-science principles + teacher PD [= row 143, 'TPD for curricula']; (c) business-as-usual control. Subject = middle-school science (STEM), grades 7-8, units Cells (fall G7), Matter (fall G8), Earth (spring G8). 2.5-day summer PD + 4x2-hr PLCs/yr over 2 yrs (34 hr). Impacts estimated with 2- or 3-level HLMs adjusting for pretest (5th/6th grade state math+reading) and demographics. Designers/researchers delivered PD; no coaching.
problems: ARM->ROW MAPPING: Content (content-knowledge PD) -> row 142; Cog-sci (curriculum + cognitive-science-principles PD) -> row 143. END-OF-TREATMENT WAVE: the state science test (Table 6, both cohorts combined) is the final, standardized/independent outcome at the end of grade 8 (end of the 2-year treatment) and is extracted as the primary contrast for each arm. The last researcher-made unit test (Earth, spring G8) is also extracted as a secondary contrast (Cohort 1 and Cohort 2 reported separately; no pooled Earth model). SD LIMITATION: the article reports impact coefficients (b) and SEs but does NOT print the response-variable raw mean/SD for student outcomes in Tables 5/6 (unlike the teacher Tables 3/4). g was therefore standardized by the pooled SD reconstructed from each model's variance-decomposition components (sqrt of the summed school[/classroom]/student residual variances): state test SD = sqrt(5.15+60.95)=8.13; Earth EOU SD(C1)=sqrt(2.04+0.79+7.95)=3.28, SD(C2)=sqrt(2.57+0.49+7.63)=3.27. These are RESIDUAL (post-covariate) variances, which slightly understate the raw pooled SD the authors used (their reported Cog-sci-vs-control end-of-unit ESs span 0 to 0.20; my reconstruction reproduces this within rounding except Matter ~0.23-0.25 vs the stated <=0.20 cap), so the magnitudes here are modest OVER-estimates (g a few % too large). The exact figure-plotted ESs (Figure 3 / Figure S2) and the online supplemental tables are not numerically available in the PDF. No achievement effect was statistically significant vs control for either arm. n_t/n_c are student counts summed across both cohorts (Table 2); per-arm/per-cohort exact analytic N for each model is not separately reported. n_clusters=90 (all randomized schools; Cohort 2 retained 82). ICC not reported (do not guess).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Content arm (teacher PD to improve science content knowledge = (P)CK / content-knowledge PD)
effect_sizes.test_name: State science test (end of grade 8), both cohorts combined
effect_sizes.timepoint: end of grade 8 (end of treatment), Cohorts 1+2 pooled
effect_sizes.g_method: d = b/SD = -1.02/8.13; SD = sqrt(school var 5.15 + student var 60.95) = 8.13 from Table 6 variance decomposition (residual). J=0.9999 (df ~ n_t+n_c-2). g = J*d; g_var = J^2*(SE/SD)^2.

effect_sizes.notes: Content (content-knowledge PD) vs business-as-usual control on the state science test. Not significant. Coefficient b=-1.02 (SE 0.66); negative = favors control. SD is residual-pooled (no raw SD printed), so |g| is a small over-estimate. End-of-treatment standardized outcome.
